preamble: Rhotacization of the alveolar implosive: [ɗ] becomes [r]. Gravina (2014) reports a regular change *ɗ > r in Bura (Margi group), and a mostly word-final *ɗ > r in the Higi-group languages Kamwe (Nkafa), Kirya and Bana, where *l > r also took place. In West Chadic, Hausa turns syllable-final ɗ into the rolled r̃ as part of the coronal branch of Klingenheben's law (kaɗàa 'beat' > kar̃kàɗaa 'beat repeatedly'; Newman 1996). Elsewhere in Central Chadic *ɗ is usually kept, reduced to [ʔ], or lost.

examples.note: Gravina (2014: 51), example (22): a regular change in Bura.
